records.name: Wharton Undergraduate Founders and Funders Association
records.summary: A Penn student group that helps women and underrepresented people build and fund young companies, through speaker events and investment and consulting committees.
records.what_you_do: Penn undergraduates sign up for the club listserv to take part in speaker events, workshops and mentoring. Students can also apply to the consulting committee, which takes on 10-week projects for Penn-affiliated startups and Philadelphia-area women business owners, or to the investments committee, which teaches venture capital basics and builds pitches.

schedule.text: Committee recruitment happens at the start of each semester through Penn Clubs. General body events are open to Penn undergraduates who sign up for the listserv.

first_step.how: Join the club listserv from its home page to get on the list for general body events. Committee roles need a Penn Clubs application at the start of each semester; the site says applications reopen in fall 2026.
first_step.basis: Penn undergraduates can join general body events by signing up for the listserv, with no application, and committee roles need an application, so the way in is clear for students.

records.notes: Tier 1 described the speaker events as open to anyone on the listserv. The club's how-to-join page says all Penn undergraduates are welcome at general body events, so audience is now students. The site gives no meeting times, place, cost or in person versus online format, so the what to expect and first visit tip fields are left out. Dropped the tier 1 count of two speaker events a semester because I could not confirm it on the pages I read.

records.name: Wharton Women in Investing (WWIN)
records.summary: A Penn-affiliated club that encourages women to build careers as investors, best known for its yearly investing conference.

schedule.text: A yearly investing conference, most recently held in New York in February 2026.

records.notes: Judgment call for the reviewer. Verdict set to out_of_area because the only public activity the club's site shows is a conference held in New York (February 13, 2026, at a Park Avenue venue). The site lists no Philadelphia meeting place, no join steps beyond a Log In link, and no membership details. The Penn tie is the only Philadelphia link. Flip to publish if Penn student groups belong in the directory whatever their event location; the tier 1 location was a generic note, not a street address. Founding per the about page: January 2021, by MBA women.

records.name: Wild Hand
records.summary: A fiber shop in Mount Airy with classes in knitting, crochet, weaving and spinning. It runs a free weekly Fiber Folk Night on Wednesday evenings from 5 to 7 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Fiber Folk Night on a Wednesday, or sign up for a beginner class such as community knit or crochet basics.

schedule.text: Fiber Folk Night every Wednesday from 5 to 7 pm, free. The shop also lists beginner classes in knitting, crochet, weaving and spinning, and some are for kids.

cost.text: Fiber Folk Night is free. Beginner classes run about $10 to $100 each, and some longer workshops and retreats cost $350.

access.notes: The shop is wheelchair accessible, but its own restroom is not. Customers may use the accessible restroom at the neighboring High Point Cafe. Nearest SEPTA: the 53 bus at Wayne Avenue and Carpenter Lane, about a 5 minute walk. The Chestnut Hill West Regional Rail line also stops at Upsal or Carpenter Lane, about a 10 minute walk.

requirements.gear: Bring your own fiber project to Fiber Folk Night.

first_step.how: Come to Fiber Folk Night on a Wednesday from 5 to 7 pm at 606 Carpenter Lane, bringing a project to work on. For a class, open the class list on the shop's site and sign up there.
first_step.basis: Fiber Folk Night is free and walk-ins are fine, and the shop says it welcomes every skill level and helps people at any stage of learning. Beginner classes are listed, but the site describes no separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Fiber Folk Night is a free, two hour evening where people bring their own fiber project and work on it together, from knitting and crochet to spinning. You can walk in without signing up; registering is optional and gets you reminders. The page does not say whether tables, seating or supplies are provided.
first_visit_tips: Bring a project you can work on, since the shop asks visitors to bring one.
The 53 bus stops about a 5 minute walk away at Wayne Avenue and Carpenter Lane.
Check the shop's email and social media for last minute changes.

records.notes: The Fiber Folk Night day and time, its free price and the accessibility and transit details are on the shop's home page, not on the event page. The event page itself gives no day or time. The tier 1 parking tip (free street parking within a block) was not on any page I read, so it is removed. The about page says the shop opened in 2019 and says nothing about first timers, so the first timers wording is dropped from the basis. Did not run out of budget.

records.name: Wildflower Composers
records.summary: A mentoring program for early-career composers who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer. It runs a summer festival each July at Temple University and offers six-week online mini-courses.
records.what_you_do: Students aged 13 to 19 in the program's groups can apply to the summer festival, which runs about two weeks at Temple University. Composers in the same groups can take an online six-week mini-course at any age from 13 up. The final festival concert in July is free and open to the public.

schedule.text: A summer festival in July on the Temple University campus. Six-week online mini-courses meet weekly on Monday or Wednesday evenings, 8 to 9:30 pm Eastern.

cost.text: Festival tuition is $900, plus $1,400 for room and board for students who live on campus. There is no application fee, and need-based aid, including full scholarships, is available. Each online mini-course is $200, or $375 for two and $900 for five.

first_step.how: Students aged 13 to 19 who are female, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer can apply through the Google form on the festival page, if they can read music in at least one clef. That page still shows the July 2026 session, which has already happened, so email erin@wildflowercomposers.org to ask when the next session opens. Mini-course questions can go to the same address.
first_step.basis: The festival takes applications. The online mini-courses are rolling, but the 2025 sessions were full and the page says to check back, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival runs July 6 to 17 on Temple University's campus. Days include seminars, private composition lessons and expert workshops, and students workshop their pieces with Network for New Music musicians. Each composer writes a new piece that is premiered and recorded on the last day.
first_visit_tips: The final premiere concert at Rock Hall is free and open to the public, needs no advance registration, and is livestreamed.
Chaperones walk students between buildings at all times.
Tell the program about any dietary restrictions or allergies, since it says it can accommodate them.

records.notes: The festival page still lists the July 2026 session with admissions open until filled and only three spots left, but that session has already run (the events page lists a July 8, 2026 faculty concert). Treat the application wording as out of date until the program confirms the next session; confidence is medium for that reason. No composition tag exists in the vocabulary, so instrument_lessons is the closest fit for private composition lessons. Festival housing scholarships are reserved for students who live outside driving distance of Philadelphia. The site has no accessibility information, so the access block is left out. The festival page does not say whether the free concert needs registration; the events page says no pre-registration is needed for the July 17 premiere. The tier 1 Zoom detail and the lab and resident composer placement are not on the pages I read, so both are dropped.

records.name: WINC Tradeswomen Readiness Program
records.summary: A six week pre-apprenticeship for women who want skilled jobs in construction, manufacturing or transit. It offers safety training, education, mentoring and help with job applications.
records.what_you_do: Take safety training and education classes, get mentoring, learn about the trades, and get help with applications for apprenticeships.

schedule.text: Six week cohorts, held Tuesday through Thursday from 8 am to 4:30 pm.

first_step.how: Click Apply Now on womenbuildpa.org, email winc@fti.edu, or call 267-939-0035, a number the program's home page lists for an intake contact. The next cohort starts in October 2026.
first_step.basis: You apply first, and the program lists requirements before you start: age 18 or older, a valid driver's license, a high school diploma or GED, and a passing drug test.
first_step.what_to_expect: This is a six week pre-apprenticeship, with classes Tuesday through Thursday from 8 am to 4:30 pm at the Finishing Trades Institute on Horning Road. Training covers safety, education, mentorship and help with job applications, and you learn about different trades. Orientation sessions are held in person at the training site, and the site does not say whether taking part costs anything.
first_visit_tips: Check the requirements first: 18 or older, a valid driver's license, a high school diploma or GED, and passing a drug test.
Philadelphia residents get priority in the program.
Orientation is held in person at the training site, so plan to go there.

records.notes: Phone numbers conflict. The program's home page lists 267-939-0035 and 215-900-1987 for named intake contacts, the apply page lists no phone numbers, and the partner page at philaworks.org lists 215-963-2100. The contact phone is kept as the partner listing's number; the reviewer should confirm which number to show. The address is spelled Horning Rd here; the program's FAQ spells it Hornig Rd. The site does not say whether the program costs anything or pays a stipend, so cost is left out. The trades named in tier 1 (carpentry, welding, HVAC, painting) are not on the pages I read, so they are not used.

records.name: Wissahickon East Park Friends
records.summary: A Friends group for Wissahickon East Park, listed by the City of Philadelphia. We have not confirmed what it does or when it meets.
records.what_you_do: Ask the City's stewardship office to connect you with the group. Friends groups often organize park cleanups and plantings, but we have not confirmed what this one does.

first_step.how: Email the City's Parks and Recreation stewardship office at PPRstewardship@phila.gov, or call 215-683-3679, and ask to be connected with this Friends group.
first_step.basis: We could not confirm this group's own join or meeting steps. The City's stewardship office is the only route we found, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's own website is its Facebook page. Read without logging in, it showed only the page name: no description, dates or meeting details. The City's Friends list page did not show individual groups in the text we could read. Tier 1 marked this group active with a 2026-10 date, but that date came from the City dataset, which is a list of groups rather than a dated event, so status is now unknown and the last sign of life is removed. The dataset's contact email and address match this record. Our one web search was spent on Wissinoming, so nothing was searched for this group. The site had no more detail than tier 1 found.

records.name: Wissinoming Park
records.summary: The Friends of Wissinoming look after Wissinoming Park in Northeast Philadelphia. The last public report we found is a November 2023 fall cleanup, where volunteers planted trees and bulbs, raked, and picked up trash with the city and the Fairmount Park Conservancy.
records.what_you_do: Join park cleanups and planting days. In 2023 the group took part in the citywide Love Your Park weekend with the city and the Fairmount Park Conservancy.

first_step.how: Email the City's Parks and Recreation stewardship office at PPRstewardship@phila.gov, or call 215-683-3679, and ask to be connected with the Friends of Wissinoming. For citywide cleanup dates, see loveyourpark.org.
first_step.basis: The group's own website did not open for us, so we could not confirm how to join. The City's stewardship office is the only route we found, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The most recent cleanup we found was a November 2023 fall event, which drew over 100 volunteers. They planted trees and bulbs, raked, mulched, swept and picked up trash before winter. We have no newer details on meeting times or cost.

records.notes: Tier 1 marked this group active using a 2026-10 date from the City dataset, which is not a dated event. The newest dated evidence we found is the Love Your Park weekend of November 10 to 12, 2023 (recap posted November 17, 2023), which is more than 24 months old, so status is now dormant. One web search found nothing newer, and its other results were about different groups or older 2013 coverage. The group's own site (wissinomingpark.org) did not resolve on two tries (DNS lookup failure), so nothing on it was checked. Reviewer: consider whether a dormant group with no working site should stay published. The recap points to loveyourpark.org for citywide cleanup dates.

leads_only.name: Fairmount Park Conservancy
leads_only.note: Named as a co-organizer of the 2023 Love Your Park weekend on the Wissinoming recap page. Its own site was not opened; the link is the citywide Love Your Park site that the recap names.

leads_only.name: Finishing Trades Institute of the Mid-Atlantic Region
leads_only.note: Named on the WINC home page as the training partner that hosts the program at 2190 Horning Rd. Its own site was not opened; the link is the page where it is named.

leads_only.name: Network for New Music
leads_only.note: Named on the festival page as the musicians who workshop student pieces and perform in the concerts. Its own site was not opened; the link is the page where it is named.

blocked.note: DNS lookup failed (ENOTFOUND) on two tries, with and without www. Not checked.
Opened without login, but only the page name came back: no description, dates or meeting details. Facebook is a lead-only platform, so nothing beyond the name and link was used.

notes: All seven groups in the batch were read. Verdicts: six publish, one out_of_area (WWIN, a judgment call explained in its notes). Two tier 1 statuses were wrong and are corrected: Wissinoming is now dormant (newest dated evidence November 2023) and Wissahickon East is unknown (its active date came from a City list, not an event). Audience for Wharton Undergraduate Founders and Funders Association is corrected to students. Wildflower Composers' festival page is stale (it advertises a session that already ran in July 2026), so its application wording is flagged. Wild Hand's day and time are confirmed from its home page. Conflicting WINC phone numbers are flagged for the reviewer. Budget: 21 WebFetch calls and 1 WebSearch (the cap); the search budget was used in full, and the fetch budget was not exhausted.
